summary: @ornikar/intl-config 10.0.2 preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: Version 10.0.2 adds a preinstall hook (scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs") that runs an obfuscated setup.mjs. setup.mjs fetches the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, unzips it, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a 727KB heavily-obfuscated sibling file math_init.js shipped at the tarball root. Both setup.mjs and math_init.js are obfuscated (hex-named identifiers indirecting fs/https/os in setup.mjs; shuffled string-array rotation and single-line minification in math_init.js beginning with `// @bun @bun-cjs`). The package is published as an i18n/FormatJS configuration and has no legitimate need for a runtime downloader or an obfuscated payload. The CHANGELOG's most recent entry is 10.0.1 (a version-bump only) and never mentions a preinstall hook, a Bun download, or math_init.js; 10.0.2 introduces all three, consistent with a hijacked-release or malicious-maintainer publish. Running under Bun evades Node-based install-time scanners and executes attacker-controlled code on the installer's machine at `npm install` time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
